Optional analytics

Publisher: John Hazelton, Holistic Recruiter Club. Purpose: understand which parts of this independent portfolio demo are useful and improve the experience.

Your choice

Usage measurement begins only after you choose Allow analytics. Rejecting has no effect on the health check. You can withdraw at any time using Analytics settings on any portfolio page. A consent preference is saved on your device for six months; the journey identifier is random and kept in this tab’s session storage until the tab closes or you reject analytics.

What is collected

Allowlisted section names (including the customer case steps), action names (including case exports and filter changes without their values), active viewing time, server receipt time, random event and session IDs. The application stores no IP address or IP network in its analytics table. Full IP addresses are processed transiently by infrastructure and may appear in provider operational logs; the application does not save them in its analytics table. Infrastructure logs and backups are governed by provider retention policies and are separate from the 30-day application event retention.

The same random session links views across pages in one browser tab. No uploaded recruiting data, candidate details, filenames, typed text, search terms, URL queries, referrer, precise location or device fingerprint is included in analytics.

Storage and access

Analytics are stored in the dedicated Supabase project in the Paris region, kept for 30 days and accessible only through authorised administration. There is no public analytics reader. Supabase and the hosting provider process requests and operational logs under their own service arrangements. The fictional demo database is publicly readable and contains synthetic records only.

Active time

Time is estimated while this tab is visible and focused, with input or scrolling in the previous minute. Approximate 15-second batches can be lost when a browser closes or a request is blocked. Statistics represent consenting visits and may include automated or repeated visits.

Your rights

You can request access, deletion or clarification through John Hazelton privately; do not post personal information or IP addresses publicly. Short-lived session IDs can make locating a particular visit difficult. You may also lodge a complaint with the CNIL. Consent is the basis for optional analytics. Infrastructure security logs are separate processing; their provider terms, legal bases and transfers must be reviewed for the intended deployment. No claim of fully anonymous visitor statistics is made. Withdrawing consent stops future collection; existing events expire under the retention policy.

Updated 5 November 2026. This notice describes the implementation; it is not a compliance certification.
